test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 30 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: When is the primary deficit zero in the Government of India budget?

options.text: When the fiscal deficit is equal to the revenue deficit
When the net interest payments is equal to the revenue deficit
When the fiscal deficit is equal to the interest payment
When the revenue deficit is zero

solution:
The correct answer is __**When the fiscal deficit is equal to the interest payment**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary deficit is defined as the fiscal deficit of the current year minus interest payments on previous borrowings.
 
• **When the fiscal deficit is equal to the interest payment**, the primary deficit is zero.
 
• This implies that the government is only borrowing to pay interest on existing debt and not for other expenditures.
 
• The concept of primary deficit helps in understanding the extent to which the government is borrowing to meet expenses other than interest payments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The fiscal deficit is the difference between the total revenue and total expenditure of the government.
 
• Interest payments are a major component of the fiscal deficit, particularly for countries with high levels of debt.
 
• Managing the primary deficit is crucial for maintaining fiscal sustainability and ensuring that debt levels do not become unmanageable.
 
• A zero primary deficit indicates that the government's current income is sufficient to cover its current expenditures, excluding interest payments.
